messages:
anya: Quick sync — we need to lock scope for the runtime change PRD: customer-driven ask (GenAI search pilot) requires better p95 for short requests and more deterministic fallbacks when kernel selection fails. Proposing kernel-selection + KV-cache policy changes as one initiative, but I think we should trim scope.
sam: thanks. can you list the absolute must-haves vs nice-to-haves?
anya: must-haves: (1) deterministic kernel routing policy for <1024 tokens, (2) fallback path on kernel failure that preserves streaming, (3) KV cache invalidation semantics for prefix re-use. nice-to-haves: automated quantization profile changes, runtime-level cost routing.
jordan: from infra POV: kernel routing + KV policy overlap a lot. we can do a simple rule-engine first (stateless mapping) then a followup with dynamic metrics-based routing. keeps rollout safer.
mike: SRE note — fallback must have circuit-breaker and telemetry flags to avoid noisy errors. add a metric for fallback-rate and a rollout abort at 2% fallback spiky increase.
rita: engineering ask — the kernel selection table touches model compilation paths. we should pin model variants in config to avoid accidental cross-compile regressions. e.g. model: redwood-3b -> kernel: attn_opt_v1.
claire: customer asks: they need p95 < 220ms for short prompts (<128 tokens) and stable outputs (no >5% semantic drift). they're flexible on cost but want predictable tail latency.
anya: ok acceptance criteria draft: - p50 for <128 tokens <= 90ms (baseline+10ms) - p95 for <128 tokens <= 220ms - fallback rate < 0.5% during canary - no quality regression >5% on eval prompt set (ROUGE/BLEU + manual checks) - rollout abort if error-rate > 0.2% sustained for 5m.
sam: implementation plan (high level): 1) implement rule-based kernel routing config 2) add safe fallback path that uses generic kernel + preserves kv cache when compatible 3) KV cache policy flags: prefix_cache=true/false, ttl_ms, and explicit invalidation API 4) telemetry + perf harness.
jordan: edge cases to call out: - streaming + fallback: must not duplicate tokens or drop final chunk - model shards compiled with incompatible custom kernels - long-context eviction when TTL conflicts with prefix re-use - quantized models where kernel selection leads to small numerics drift on rare tokens
mike: rollout plan: alpha on dedicated infra -> internal e2e tests -> 1% production canary (selected orgs) -> 25% -> 100%. abort criteria: latency p95 regression >15% vs canary baseline OR fallback-rate spike >2% OR increase in error budget consumption.
rita: sample config snippet for the PRD (what we'd ship as a minimal user-visible object):
```
runtime.routing:
  kernel_policy:
    - match: seq_len <= 128
      kernel: attn_fast_v2
    - match: seq_len <= 1024
      kernel: attn_balanced_v1
    - default:
      kernel: attn_generic
  fallback:
    strategy: generic_stream_preserve
kv_cache:
  prefix_cache: true
  ttl_ms: 300000
  invalidation_endpoint: /runtime/kv/invalidate
```
sam: that looks good. we should also include a compatibility matrix with model families and quantization formats in the PRD. keeps rollout engineers honest.
anya: prioritized acceptance checklist (we'll ship only items above): - rule-based kernel_policy config - fallback strategy implemented and tested - KV prefix_cache + invalidation API - perf harness and eval suite run with canary - update console to show per-route fallback and kernel selection metrics
claire: customers want an opt-out flag per-route so they can disable new kernel policies until they validate outputs. please add `kernel_policy_opt_out: true|false`.
rita: added to config.
jordan: tests to include: unit test for routing table, fuzz tests on seq_len boundaries, integration test for streaming fallback (simulate mid-stream kernel failure), end-to-end evaluation against eval set.
mike: monitoring: p50/p95 latency per model+route, fallback_rate, fallback_latency_delta, error_rate, user-visible consistency failures (manual flagging). set alerts: p95 > 250ms OR fallback_rate > 1% sustained 10m.
anya: scope negotiation point — product wanted cost-routing in same PRD. we should push cost-routing to v2. it's orthogonal and increases blast radius. everyone ok?
sam: agree. keep cost-routing v2.
jordan: ok. also recommend adding a 'dry-run' mode: apply kernel_policy but log decision without enforcing for 24h. helps surface incompatibilities.
rita: good call — we'll add `enforce: false|true` on policy.
claire: timeline ask from customer: wants initial canary in ~6 weeks. realistic?
sam: tight but doable if we scope to rule-based routing + fallback + kv invalidation + tests. 6 weeks for alpha -> 2 weeks for canary.
anya: I'll update the PRD with the trimmed scope and acceptance criteria and post RFC draft by EOD tomorrow. action items: @sam create repo branch + draft design doc, @rita sketch config schema, @jordan enumerate compatibility matrix, @mike write monitoring/alert playbook.
rita: noted. starting config schema now.
deploy-bot: reminder — RFC template created: /docs/rfcs/2026/runtime-kernel-kv-policy.md
sam: SGTM. thanks all.
claire: :thumbsup:
anya: closing thread — will link PRD + RFC once uploaded.
